body:
## Observation

CAGRA batch search (multi-CTA kernel path) returns measurably **lower recall@10 than single-query search (single-CTA path) on the same resident graph, same K** — reproducible, sign-consistent.

Measured during the #98 benchmark (VM `pg-cuvs-item2b`, A100-SXM4-80GB DGX, cuVS 26.04, ext 0.6.0, wiki_all_1M 1M×768, gd=32/igd=128/ivf_pq, 2000 queries, k=10):

| scale | K | single recall@10 | batch recall@10 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1M | 200 | 0.99295 | 0.9907 | -0.00225 |
| 1M | 200 | 0.9932 | 0.9907 | -0.0025 |
| 1M | 200 | 0.9932 | 0.9907 | -0.0024 |
| 100k | 64 | 0.9814 | 0.9824 | **+0.0010** (sign flips) |

- Batch recall is **exactly 0.9907 in all three 1M probes** (batch path deterministic); single varies slightly.
- Corroboration that this is the cuVS kernel, not pg_cuvs's shm/IPC path: the **raw cuVS batch arm** (python `cuvs.neighbors.cagra`, no Postgres) also lands at 0.9892 at 1M — lower than raw single-loop, same direction.
- Tooling: `bench/cuvs_bench_backend/same_graph_delta.py` reproduces this in ~2 min on a resident index.

## Suspected mechanism

`sparams.algo` is left AUTO in both wrapper paths (`src/cuvs_wrapper.cu:1116-1130` single vs `:1211-1220` batch); cuVS AUTO picks single-CTA vs multi-CTA by batch size. The two kernels have different search trajectories, so recall is not expected to be bit-identical — but a consistent ~0.002-0.0025 deficit for multi-CTA at 1M/K=200 is a measurable quality gap, and the sign flip vs 100k/K=64 means the gap is scale- and/or K-dependent (both variables changed between the two calibrations; not isolated).

## Why recorded

The #98 harness originally hard-gated |batch-single| recall at a 100k-calibrated tolerance; the 1M run tripped it (0.0021 > 0.0020). Investigation confirmed same-graph reproducibility → the gate was downgraded to observe-and-record per its pre-registered fallback, with a coarse tripwire (|delta| > 0.01) kept for gross errors. Both recalls are now recorded side by side; batch QPS headlines carry batch's own recall.

Possibly relevant upstream (cuVS multi-CTA recall behavior) — may be worth raising via the NVIDIA/cuVS channel with these numbers.

## Not in scope

No behavior change requested yet. Candidate directions if this matters for 3M users: expose `search_algo` as a GUC so batch callers can force single-CTA; or document the expected batch recall delta. Either belongs to a separate decision.
title: observation: CAGRA batch (multi-CTA) recall consistently ~0.002 below single-query on the same graph at 1M
